Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the second innings. The umpires are on the field and the West Indies players run out on the field. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja walk out to open the innings and it will be Steven Smith on strike. Kemar Roach has the new pink ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Australia, on the other hand, were pretty dominant early on and were quick to send half of their opposite back to the hut without much on the board. However, they failed to build on that and the conditions became a bit easy to bat as well. Lyon finally broke that big partnership and then the pacers made good progress with the second new ball to expose the tail. They did concede a few too many runs, but we're able to restrict their opponents. Starc was the pick of the bowlers and also reached the milestone of 350 Test wickets. They were gifted a run-out where Kemar Roach had to walk back to the pavilion which brought morale back in their side. Nathan Lyon took the last wicket as he tempted Kevin Sinclair to step out of his crease and Alex Carey behind the stumps took off the bails. It is now up to the batters to put up a strong innings and try to get a comfortable lead.

The top order of the Windies failed once again and they were reeling at 64/5. While Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kirk Mckenzie got off to decent starts but couldn't make the most of it. It was then that magnificent 149-run partnership between Kevin Sinclair and Joshua Da Silva that took them out of that miserable situation. In the process, both of them registered their respective half-centuries as well, but both got dismissed in their 70s as well. After that, Alzarri Joseph played a counter-attacking knock of 32 runs off just 22 balls which included seven boundaries. He was well supported by debutant Kevin Sinclair who stayed out for a long time. He built another strong-looking partnership with Kemar Roach. Roach was dismissed due to miscommunication but Kevin Sinclair continued to bat long and tried to take the aggressive approach. He got to his half-century as well but was stumped soon after. 311 runs on the board for West Indies and it is the second-highest score by a visiting team in a Day/Night test match in Australia. It is now up to the bowlers to analyze the conditions well and try to get some quick wickets.

OUT! STUMPED! Fifty and out for Kevin Sinclair and that is it! Nathan Lyon tosses this one nicely, outside off, turns in a bit, Kevin Sinclair skips down the track to the leg side and tries to push it away, but loses his balance and misses it, Alex Carey behind the stumps fails to collect it on the first attempt, but has enough time to grab it on the second attempt and takes the bails off. West Indies have been bowled out for 311!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 2! There was a bit of drizzle around earlier but that has stopped and we are beginning on time. The players are already out in the middle now. After that wicket of Alzarri Joseph just before Stumps, Kemar Roach joins Kevin Sinclair at the crease for West Indies. Josh Hazlewood to complete his over to start proceedings here. Let's play...

West Indies had a lot to take from the First Day. The openers laid a strong foundation but couldn't take the innings deep. Kavem Hodge and Joshua Da Silva took things in their own hands and tired out everyone from the Aussie side in the second session. They put up a strong stand and put up a good score on the board, reaching their half centuries along the way. In the third session, they lost a couple of wickets but Alzarri Joseph took the aggressive route and took the bowlers to the cleaners. The Day ended with his wicket. Usman Khawaja, the newly named 2023 ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year is up for a chat. He says that he has known about the award for a week. Adds that it was an interesting year for him and the team. Talks about how the Ashes was special for him. Mentions that he has worked hard to play against spin and mentions that the innings he played in Dubai a few years ago was a big confidence booster for him.

Joshua Da Silva and Kavem Hodge came out to bat after the Dinner break and continued from where they left off in the previous session. They increased the scoring rate and both of them brought up their respective fifties with Hodge registering his first in Test cricket. They saw out till the end of the session solidly and extended the partnership. Pat Cummins stuck with Nathan Lyon and got his reward when he trapped Joshua Da Silva in front of the stumps to break the fantastic 149-run partnership. Mitchell Starc was given the second new ball and he removed Kavem Hodge to pick his fourth wicket as both the set batters went back in their 70s. The Aussies were hoping to build on that and remove the tail quickly, but that was not the case at all. Alzarri Joseph and Kevin Sinclair counter-attacked excellently and took the opportunity to score quick runs with the new ball. They played a few lusty blows especially Joseph who scored a quick-fire 32 off just 22 balls with seven boundaries, but it was his ultra-attacking intent that led to his downfall in the last over before Stumps.

The second session was all about the terrific fightback from West Indies. Joshua Da Silva and Kavem Hodge took responsibility and were rock solid with the bat throughout that session. They judged the deliveries well and did not get tempted to throw their bats at anything. While being sensible, they did not go into their shell; they rotated the strike well and put away the loose balls to release the pressure on them. Together, they added 81 runs and saw the entire session out without losing any more wickets.

Australia after being asked to bowl first, started off brilliantly in the first session. Their opening pace duo of Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc piled up the pressure on the batters before the former finally drew first blood. They then let the batters settle in for a bit, and Pat Cummins broke that stand with a nice set up. However, then it was all about Mitchell Starc who picked up his 350th Test wicket and ended the session with two more to send half the Windies team back in the hut before Tea.

A riveting Day 1 comes to an end! Session Summary - 121 runs and 3 wickets in 37 overs. It all started with Australia's dominance with the ball led by Mitchell Starc. Then we saw West Indies come back in this game with an exceptional partnership between Kavem Hodge and Joshua Da Silva while in the third session, both teams went hard at each other with the hosts just edging it in the end. All of this action unfolded in front of a record crowd at Gabba for a Test against the Windies.

The Aussies were brilliant with their lines and lengths in the first session but then kind of lost their rhythm after Tea. Cameron Green and Mitchell Marsh bowled tight short spells individually but they couldn’t manage to give any breakthroughs to the team. Nathan Lyon also had nothing to beat the batters as they managed to read the spinner quite well. The batters, Joshua Da Silva and Kavem Hodge batted with patience and didn’t play any poor shots. They had answers to everything the bowlers threw at them Marnus Labuschagne was introduced just before the break and he too failed to provide a breakthrough. Will the pink ball offer something more to the pacers under the lights? Will Australia bounce back in the final session for the first day? Everything will unfold in a short while. Join us back for Session 3 of Day 1 at 2.30 pm IST (9.00 am GMT).

Mitchell Marsh is up for a chat he says that he got a bit bored only fielding in this session. Adds that it is a really good wicket for batting but hopes that their bowlers can get help under the lights in the next session. Tells that it has been a long time since he last played a Day/Night Test. Mentions that at Adelaide there is a lot of grass which keeps the pink ball hard for longer but that is not the case here. Ends by saying that they will look to get the breakthroughs in the last session.

A remarkable fight back in the second session from West Indies! The second session of Day 1 resumed with Kavem Hodge and Joshua Da Silva out in the middle for the Windies. They had a tough hill to climb ahead of them. First, to stabilize the innings and not lose any more wickets. Then, to put some runs on the board and bat as long as possible to tire out the Aussies. They managed to tick both the boxes as these two batted sensibly and with a good temperament. They attacked the poor deliveries, respected the good ones, and left the balls that were meant to tempt them. Kavem Hodge and Joshua Da Silva, both made sure to keep rotating the strike and didn’t let the bowlers put them under pressure while they were stranded at one end. The pitch has turned out to be easier to bat on now and they have another session left for the day to put some more runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! An important session for the visitors as this might dictate the pathway for them going ahead in the game. The side though needs to be a bit more pro-active in terms of strike rotation and playing the ball to its merit as they missed out on a lot of scoring opportunities prior to Tea. The Windies openers took a cautious approach and the run-scoring was difficult for them. The skipper Kraigg Brathwaite struggled throughout his knock and was ultimately put out of his misery by Josh Hazlewood. Kirk Mckenzie and Tagenarine Chanderpaul steadied the ship for a bit but just as when they were looking settled, Kirk Mckenzie chased a wide delivery and threw his wicket to Pat Cummins. Chanderpaul was looking solid, but it was Mitchell Starc who removed him for 21, the same score as McKenzie. Start then dismissed Alick Athanaze to get his 350th Test wicket, and he also got the wicket for Kavem Hodge to finish the session. West Indies are reeling at 64/5 and desperately needs a partnership after Tea while the Aussies will look to wrap things up quickly. The second session starts at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT), so join us then for all the action.

Pat Cummins is up for a quick chat. He says it is really impressive for Mitchell Starc to get his 350th wicket which is a lot. Adds that Starc always trains hard, and is one of the most resilient bowlers, and always wants to play, sometimes even when he should not. Tells that everyone in the team is well-prepared and tries to grab their chances. Mentions that they wanted to take advantage of the pink ball early on as it gets softened quickly.

SESSION SUMMARY - 64 runs and 5 wickets in 25.2 overs. A dominating session from the Aussies! The highlight of the session was Mitchell Starc's 350th Test wicket, but the others also contributed well as the Aussies extended their good bowling record with the pink ball. West Indies once again have been disappointed with the bat as they have lost half their side in this first session without much on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin at the Gabba! The umpires are already out in the middle while we see the Australian players spread out and take their respective field positions. Australia (Unchanged Playing XI) - Usman Khawaja, Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Kirk Mckenzie, Alick Athanaze, Kavem Hodge, Justin Greaves, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Kevin Sinclair (In place of Gudakesh Motie & On Debut), Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Kemar Roach.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Kraigg Brathwaite and West Indies have elected to BAT first.

The visitors performed well with the ball in the 2nd innings. Shamar Joseph, on his debut clinched a five-wicket haul and even scored valuable runs off his bat. Kirk Mckenzie was also in good rhythm but he will need to take the innings deep. The other batters did not rise to the occasion and under performed. They will need to be at their best while facing Australia at the Gabba. They will need to bat longer and tire out the Aussie bowlers. This is expected to be a thrilling contest but the weather might just play a role in this game. Hopefully, the rain god show mercy and don't interrupt this game. The Aussies have taken the early lead after winning the previous one by 10 wickets. Steven Smith was the new opening partner for Usman Khawaja. In the first Test, Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood put the pressure early on in the first innings by taking 4 wickets each. In the batting unit, Travis Head scored a fine century but they too couldn't gain much of a lead. In the third innings, Hazlewood clinched a fifer and cleaned up the visitors for 120. After that, it was a cake walk for the hosts and they clinched a comfortable 10 wicket win in just three days. Australia have never lost a Day/Night Test and will be looking to maintain that record.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. The Australian Test summer is on it's peak and all the attention now shifts to the Gabba in Brisbane where Australia and West Indies clash for the 2nd test and the only Day/Night Test in this series. This stadium will be hosting its first Pink-Ball Test in five years and we hope it will be exciting as ever.
